extracted.intended_audience: researchers, research administrators, policy-makers and the interested public seeking an overview of Inserm's research activities and ethical/operational principles
extracted.subtask_description: An institutional overview of Inserm's research activities across fundamental, clinical, public health and technology domains, together with the ethical, translational and methodological principles that guide that work. The page summarises topic pages (clinical trials, scientific integrity, animal use, participatory research, etc.) rather than giving detailed procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inserm and Clinical Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Inserm participates in many clinical trials in France; sponsors (entities assuming responsibility) are often public research organisations or hospitals (academic research) or pharmaceutical companies. Inserm is currently responsible for 250 research projects, 150 of which are sponsored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises institutional responsibility for clinical research and the variety of sponsoring organisations; implies expectation that sponsors assume regulatory and ethical responsibility for trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trials (Interventional studies on a health product)
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of a clinical trial on a health product (medicinal product, device, or cell and gene therapy) is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of the product in healthy volunteers or patient volunteers; the medicinal product may subsequently obtain marketing authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames clinical trials as safety and efficacy evaluations leading to regulatory outcomes (marketing authorization). Implies compliance with applicable regulatory pathways and ethical standards for volunteer participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific integrity comprises all rules and values that must govern research to ensure its honesty and scientific rigor; it is essential for maintaining society’s trust in research stakeholders and is an ongoing consideration across all areas of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions integrity as a cross-cutting, continuous obligation: honesty, rigor, and adherence to ethical/deontological norms. The page signals institutional attention to integrity but does not list procedural details here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value Creation and Transfer of New Discoveries
rubrics_metrics.description: One of Inserm’s core missions is to capitalise on scientists’ research by accelerating translation from laboratory discoveries to patient benefit, combining academic approaches with industrial strategies to transform discoveries, inventions and know‑how into innovations for society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights the translational objective (bench-to-bedside), fostering partnerships and strategies that enable diagnostic tests, therapeutic innovations, and other societal applications of research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Health technology research covers technological developments essential to biomedical progress on both fundamental and clinical levels; it concerns five major fields: imaging; technologies associated with drug development; biotechnology and bioengineering; surgery and other interventional techniques; and related technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the thematic scope of technology research and indicates that technological development spans from basic understanding to clinical application; suggests interdisciplinary and field-specific methodological expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamental research expands understanding in life and health sciences; it is primarily a source of knowledge and exploratory work whose results can be unpredictable yet can reveal novel concepts that drive progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames basic research as exploratory and high‑value for generating novel concepts; implies tolerance for uncertainty in methods and outcomes and the primacy of knowledge generation over immediate application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Continuum
rubrics_metrics.description: Research begins from existing knowledge, with scientists asking questions, constructing hypotheses and developing experiments that generate new knowledge; Inserm is involved across this continuum (from benchtop to bedside) to transform advances into progress in human health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises the full pathway from hypothesis formation to application, underscoring coherence across stages and the expectation of translational intent where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Animals for Research Purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Animals are used as models because of their scientific validity to understand diseases and develop treatments; this use raises ethical questions and warrants social debate, and Inserm recognises its responsibilities when using animal models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals ethical responsibility and the need for justification and oversight when using animals in research; although procedural details are not provided here, the emphasis is on balancing scientific validity with ethical considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participatory Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Participatory research gives citizens a role alongside researchers in the production of knowledge and innovation; citizen science and participatory approaches involve stakeholders in diverse forms across scientific fields and aim to make science responsive to societal issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages stakeholder involvement and co‑production of knowledge, implying methodologies that engage citizens and adapt to varied formats and fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Health Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Public health research aims to understand determinants of population health and to propose interventions and health policies based on scientific evidence to improve health, well‑being and reduce health inequalities; Inserm hosts over 110 teams dedicated to public health research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises evidence‑based policy and intervention design, population‑level outcomes and equity considerations as central evaluative aims for public health research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical and Deontological Practices (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The site directs readers to pages describing activities carried out in laboratories, as well as the good ethical and deontological practices implemented at Inserm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that institutional expectations include specific ethical and deontological guidelines governing research conduct; while details are on linked pages, the presence of these practices is a stated institutional standard.
